signal: Bitsight launched Identity Intelligence off its Cybersixgill acquisition

email.body1:
Zachary, saw Bitsight shipped Identity Intelligence, the first new solution off the Cybersixgill acquisition.

A new module usually means a fresh wave of accounts to work, and that is exactly when follow-up volume outpaces what a rep can do by hand. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so each rep covers 3-5x more accounts without burning the day on research and CRM.

I built a personalized signal play for Bitsight off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Zachary, quick follow-up for Bitsight.

Most SDRs lose deals not on the first touch but on follow-up they never get to, since manual research and writing eat the hours. Tightening the sequence is usually the fastest lift before you ever add headcount.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50-70%, and I'll show you where Bitsight's sequence is leaving replies on the table.
email.body3:
Zachary, last bit of proof for Bitsight.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Bitsight's reply rate likely compares to other security startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Zachary, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting follow-up load and ramp time isn't a priority right now, no problem at all. I know post-launch the queue only gets longer, not shorter.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an SDR team? I'll tailor it to Bitsight either way.
